title: Predictive Reserved Credit Model with Sliding Replenishment Probe
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Hypothesis: For streaming-heavy enterprise customers, offering a predictive reserved credit product (prepaid token pool that auto-replenishes based on recent consumption signals with a sliding replenishment window) will reduce billing surprise, smooth traffic spikes, and increase commit utilization while preserving per-token revenue. This probe will validate pricing elasticity, operational complexity, and SQ/security acceptability for enterprise contracts.
experiment_design: We will run a 12-week randomized pilot with two cohorts: Control (standard per-token + streaming pricing with existing minimums) and Treatment (Predictive Reserved Credits). Treatment customers purchase a baseline reserved credit bucket (e.g., 1M token credits) with an SLA-backed replenishment rule: when utilization over the last 60m exceeds 70% of bucket, auto-replenish by configured tranche (e.g., 25% of bucket) up to a monthly cap. Pricing model for treatment: 15% discount on streaming ingress tokens, 10% discount on egress, with a soft monthly minimum equal to 20% of reserved bucket. We'll instrument billing service to create virtual 'commit balance' and track commit utilization ratio. Cohort assignment will prioritize customers with >60% streaming traffic and enterprise SQ in progress.
metrics: Net Revenue per Customer (NRPC) - compare cohorts
Effective Cost Per Delivered Token (ECPT) - server-side realized cost weighted by token direction
Billing Surprise Score - percent of invoices with >25% month-over-month variance
Commit Utilization Ratio - fraction of reserved credits actually consumed
Streaming Tail Latency SLO breaches - 99.9th percentile latency for streaming requests
Churn / Contract Renegotiation events within 90 days
Support Contact Rate for billing questions
acceptance_criteria: Treatment NRPC >= Control NRPC - 5% (allow small variance)
Billing Surprise Score reduced by at least 40% for treatment
No statistically significant increase in streaming 99.9th percentile latency
Security questionnaire path documented and accepted by two reference customers
rollout_plan: Week 0-2: Implementation - billing service flags, UI for configuring reserved buckets in Console
Week 3: Internal alpha with two QA customers (non-revenue) to validate replenishment and bill generation
Week 4-6: Pilot onboarding - 20 enterprise customers split across control/treatment
Week 7-12: Measure and iterate (pricing tweaks at week 9 if utilization low)
Post-week 12: Decide ramp to beta / productize or rollback
telemetry: console:customer-facing balance history widget - track customer queries
security_questionnaire_notes: Enterprise SQ asks for auditability of billing, replenishment triggers, and dispute workflows. Draft answers: 1) Billing logs: all replenishment events and token burns are logged to audit-log topic and retained 1 year. 2) Dispute process: manual review + automated delta check, engage Revenue Ops. 3) Data handling: no PII in billing payloads; token hashes stored. KMS integration for billing data snapshots available. Attachments: confluence.redwood.ai/display/SQ/Billing+Answers+Draft+2026-03 (internal). Need legal to review auto-replenish clause for contract language.
